text:
taylor wong: Heads-up: the new edge sample started throwing weird TS inference after we switched the bundle step to esbuild + swc for faster builds. Generics that used to work are resolving to `any` or `unknown` depending on the consumer.

nina ahmed: ugh that sounds nasty. any repro?

taylor wong: minimal case attached inline:
```ts
// client.d.ts (what consumers see)
export declare function fetchRecord<T extends Record<string, any>>(id: string): Promise<T>;

// after bundling to ESM + .d.ts rollup, consumers see:
const rec = await client.fetchRecord({foo: 1});
rec.foo // TS: Property 'foo' does not exist on type 'any' OR 'unknown' depending on config
```

cal eb: two common culprits: (1) package.json `exports`/`types` pointing to wrong d.ts, causing TS to pick the fallback declaration. (2) build tool rewriting type-only imports so overload resolution loses context.

build-bot: CI: sample-edge/ci #117 — tsc --noEmit failed in browser bundle step

ming xu: We also saw `moduleResolution` and `assumeChangesOnlyAffectDirectDependencies` differences across TS versions. For edge samples using modern bundlers, `moduleResolution: 'bundler'` helps. For vercel/esbuild flows, `moduleResolution: 'node16'` is more stable.

nina ahmed: Another weirdness: overloads + generic defaults. If we publish multiple overloads then some bundlers import the non-generic fallback signature in .d.ts. That widens to `unknown`. Avoid multiple overloads?

taylor wong: I tried removing overloads and switching to a single generic with conditional types — inference improved in both Node & Edge. But breaking change risk for downstream callers.

product-dx: For DX could we add a companion `fetchRecordTyped<T>()` helper so callers can be explicit until we stabilize types? That keeps ergonomics.

ming xu: yep `fetchRecordTyped<T>` is low friction. Also add small docs blurb: "If you see 'Property X does not exist on type unknown', try specifying the generic or using `as const` on literals."

cal eb: action items I propose:
- audit package.json `types`/`exports` entries for sample packages (ensure .d.ts paths are correct)
- add a small CI job: build sample ESM bundle then run `tsc --noEmit` with TS v5.x matrix
- avoid overload-heavy typings in SDK root; provide explicit `*Typed` helpers and a migration note
- document edge vs node auth retry differences (edge uses fetch + short-lived token flow; node uses cached token + agent)

build-bot: Issue created: #2460 — edge-sample-types-ci-failure

nina ahmed: small nit: don't recommend `skipLibCheck` in samples. It hides problems. If needed for short term, leave a comment why and open a follow-up to fix proper declarations.

taylor wong: I'm going to open two PRs: one for sample-app tsconfig + CI matrix, another for SDK helper `fetchRecordTyped` and a typings cleanup RFC. Assigning ming to review.

ming xu: I'll review. also add a tiny unit test that imports the published .d.ts in a fake consumer project (ts-node or ts-patch) to catch packaging regressions.

product-dx: I'll add a short Quickstart note about typical TS friction (moduleResolution, exports/types, overloads) and link the helper. Should cut down support tickets.

cal eb: nice. one more detail: check `typesVersions` in package.json — sometimes we ship different overloads per TS range and that can cause unexpected resolution. Prefer a single stable surface for now.

taylor wong: great catch. will check. thanks all — will drop PR links here when ready. :rocket:
